patches.from: A colocation service (housing) is a service in which the user places the communication equipment or servers that the user owns into a rack inside the service provider's building (a data center), where they are installed and operated. patches.from: A project charter is a document created at the startup (beginning) of a project to declare that the project has been formally approved. It states the purpose and objectives of the project — the answer to «why are we doing this project» — the expected results, the high-level requirements, and the appointment of the project manager together with the authority granted to that person. The phrase in the question, «in order to comprehensively manage and coordinate the project's activities», also refers to setting an overall direction that runs through the whole project, not to the details of individual tasks. Therefore the appropriate content to include in the charter is «エ The purpose of the project». Only when the purpose is clear can the later detailed plans, such as the schedule and the organizational structure, be drawn up without drifting off course.

patches.from: The correct answer is ウ ((1) SMTP, (2) POP3, (3) SMTP). In (1), the mail client sends mail out to its own mail server, and the protocol used for sending is SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol). In (3), mail servers relay mail from one to another; this is also a «sending» action from server to server, so SMTP is used here as well. On the other hand, (2) is the case where the mail client goes to the mail server to pick up the mail addressed to it, so POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3), the protocol for receiving (retrieving), is used. In short, the rule is «SMTP for every sending direction, POP3 only for the receiving direction», so ウ with (1) SMTP, (2) POP3, (3) SMTP matches the figure.

patches.from: Because the data is sorted in descending order by the sales figures in column B before the running total is taken, column I (cumulative sales composition ratio) grows larger the further down the rows you go; it is a monotonically increasing value. The choice that has this form is IF(I2≦0.7,'A',IF(I2≦0.9,'B','C')), which is «ア»; copying it to J3 through J11 correctly derives each row's rank from its cumulative value.

patches.from: The correct answer is イ, COUNTIF(B$2 ~ B$36, = $A40). In spreadsheets, $ means «make that part an absolute reference (it does not move when the formula is copied)», while a part without $ is a relative reference and shifts automatically by the direction and distance of the copy. In this question, the formula entered in B40 is copied both to the right (column B → column G) and downward (row 40 → row 50), so for the range and for the condition you only need to ask «in which direction do I want it to shift?». The first argument, the range to be counted, is rows 2 to 36 of columns B to G, where each student's score for each class is stored. When copied to the right, the column should shift as class P (column B) → class Q (column C) → … → class U (column G), so the column is relative (it stays as B); when copied downward, the target must always stay in rows 2 to 36, so the rows are absolute ($2, $36) ⇒ B$2 ~ B$36. The score referred to by the second argument, the condition, is in rows 40 to 50 of column A. When copied downward, the row should shift as 0 points → 1 point → … → 10 points, so the row is relative (40); even when copied to the right, the score must always be read from column A, so the column is absolute ($A) ⇒ $A40. The formula is therefore COUNTIF(B$2 ~ B$36, = $A40). For example, copying this formula to D42 gives COUNTIF(D$2 ~ D$36, = $A42), which correctly counts how many students in class R (column D) scored 2 points.

S/MIME is a standard that uses public-key cryptography to encrypt and digitally sign the MIME-format body and the attachments of an email themselves. The sender encrypts the content with the public key of the intended recipient, so only that recipient, who holds the matching private key, can decrypt it. The content stays as ciphertext while the mail is relayed through mail servers and while it is stored on them, so it exactly meets the requirement that «only the recipient specified in the destination can read the content» (end-to-end encryption). At the same time, the signature also prevents impersonation of the sender and detects tampering.
